findings.quote: Bjorkedals orgel skulle bara hela forsamlingens sang, medan Torebys efter ombyggnaden mest tjanade organistens spel.
findings.note: A and B are direct inversions of each other (Bjorkedal<->congregation vs Bjorkedal<->organist) - the classic mirror-pair tell that brackets the key. C ('inte langre spela nagra psalmer over huvud taget') is an absolute overstatement and D ('en och samme byggmastare') is an off-target similarity, not the emphasized musical difference; both are form-eliminable as filler. Blind I can drop C and D (2+ eliminations) and narrow to the A/B pair but cannot decide direction without the passage, so the key is not isolated to one option by form -> PARTIALLY, flag not kill.

findings.quote: Varje kyrkorgel är byggd för att församlingen ska sjunga med, aldrig för att lyssnas till.
findings.note: B falls at once as a 'varje ... aldrig' absolute, and on an 'överensstämmer bäst med texten' stem the only general thesis statement (C) is favoured over the two dated particulars. But A and D are ordinary specific claims with no form defect and either could be what the text states, so the item is only partly decided blind.

findings.quote: Båda orglarna byggdes av en och samme byggmästare, fast för skilda församlingar.
findings.note: Two options fall on the stem's own terms: D states a similarity where the stem asks for a difference, and C is an 'inte längre ... över huvud taget' absolute. A and B are exact mirror images of one another, so which organ served which purpose is genuinely undecidable without the passage - better than chance, no pick.

findings.quote: Svinnet steg troligen, mest hos de yngre barnen och främst vid de varma rätterna.
findings.note: B is absolute on two axes ('Alla elever ... alldeles oavsett vilken rätt'), and A inverts the trial's logic (schools choosing the delivered food is not a result a waste trial could show). C stays substantive so the item is not decided, but the hedged specific option is the visible key shape blind.
